ZONINGLOTANDDEVELOPMENTDECLARATION nuH February, 2016 (this “Declaration"), by 14 White Street LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, having an address at 34 Monroe Place, Apartment 6B, Brooklyn, N.Y. 11201 RECITALS: A. Owner is the fee owner of certain real property, together with the buildings and improvements located thereon, located in the Borough of Manhattan, City, County and State of New York, known as Tax Lot 8.in Block 191 on the Tax Map of the City of New York, County of New York, more particularly described on Exhibit A attached hereto and made a part hereof (the “Real Property"; the buildings and improvements located thereon herein referred to as the "ExistingImprovements"). B. Owner desires to sub-divide the Real Property into two separate tax lots (the “Tax (the “Limiting Plane") more particularly described on Exhibit B attached hereto and made a part hereof (the “Fee_Below the Plane"), and (i) a single tax lot, which shall include the Excess Development Rights (defined below), to be located above the Limiting Plane more particularly described on Exhibit C attached hereto and made a part hereof (the “Fee Above the Plane"), in each case, as depicted on Exhibit D attached hereto and made a part hereof; C。 Following the approval of the Tax Lot Subdivision by the Department of Finiance of The City of New York and the Department of Buildings of The City of New York (the “Tax Lot Subdivision Approval"), (i) the Fee Above the Plane shall be known as Tax Lot 90o8 in Block 191 on the Tax Map of the City of New York, County of New York, and (i) the Fee Below the Plane shall be known as Tax Lot 8 in Block 191 on the Tax Map of the City of New York,County of NewYork. D. The Real Property constitutes a single “zoning lot" as such term is defined in Section 12-10 of the Zoning Resolution of the City of New York, effective December 15, 1961 (as amended to date, the “Zoning Resolution"). E. As used herein “Floor Area Development Rights" shall mean the rights as determined in accordance with and subject to the bulk, use, parking, and other requirements of the Zoning Resolution appurtenant to a zoning lot to (x) develop such zoning lot by erecting thereon building(s) or other structure(s) with a total floor area that is the sum of (i) the product of the area of the zoning lot and the basic maximum allowable floor area ratio for structures in the zoning district in which the zoning lot is located, and (i) any bonus floor area available to the zoning lot under the Zoning Resolution, (y) locate within such structures or on the zoning lot such uses, including accessory uses, and dwelling units as are permitted under the Zoning Resolution, and (z) seek discretionary and administrative approvals under the Zoning Resolution from the applicableNewYork City governmental agencies.
